How installments and outside interest are calculated

Your selected rule: each row is a separate payout scenario. Total installments paid = amount received. Monthly installment = amount received ÷ 20. For a ₹40,00,000 face value and ₹12,70,000 auction discount including commission, you receive ₹27,30,000 and pay ₹1,36,500 per month for 20 months, totaling ₹27,30,000. The discount is not charged again as interest. Interest / cost paid is therefore zero under this rule.

Outside lending rate is annual: 12% means 1% per month. Month 1 has 19 full months remaining until month 20. Lending ₹27,30,000 at 12% earns ₹27,300 per month, or ₹5,18,700 over 19 months. Principal plus outside interest is ₹32,48,700. Net gain = this amount − ₹27,30,000 total installments = ₹5,18,700.

The full payout stays lent out, interest does not compound, and principal is returned at the end. Installments are paid separately, not withdrawn from the lent principal. Month 20 earns no outside interest in this comparison. Taxes and missed repayments are excluded.

Months 1–19: payout = face value − bid, with organizer commission included in the bid. Month 20: payout = face value − bid − organizer commission. Commission is a percentage of face value. Changing face value scales current bids proportionally; individual bids remain editable. This uses the installment rule you selected rather than calculating actual monthly auction dividends.

Net % = net gain ÷ payout × 100. Monthly net % = Net % ÷ 20; annual net % = monthly net % × 12. These are simple comparison figures, not IRR. Rankings use unrounded Net %. With equal payout and total paid, this ranking depends on the outside rate and months remaining, so earlier payouts rank higher when the rate is positive.

How these estimates work

EMI uses a fixed annual rate, monthly reducing-balance interest and month-end payments. Extra payments start in month one and shorten the term. Fees, taxes and penalties are excluded unless explicitly entered. Flat interest uses the original principal throughout. Loan comparison measures total cash paid, not APR or present value.

Chit figures cover one auction. Organizer commission is included in the auction discount; the remaining discount is shared equally among all members, including the winner. Members equal installments. Actual scheme rules can differ, and future discounts are unknown.
